correctness.rationale: Rescaling nonzero triangular diagonal entries transforms the idempotent equations to additive triangular Frobenius equations. Nondegenerate finite-field trace pairing makes every new restriction a uniform F2-linear functional; its kernel dimension gives the exact transition probabilities and every field-size-independent atom. The conditional first/second moment recurrences yield E K=n and Var K=binomial(n,2), with extreme events computed by multiplying conditional probabilities. The directly evaluated finite-field checker exhaustively enumerates 36,033 labeled matrices and their vectors in 11 field/dimension cases; it is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 survey proves only the full-GL mean-one result (Remark 23) and asks about sparse random evolution algebras (Question 22), not the complete uniform upper-triangular binary-field law. The triangular law has mean n and forbids zero nonzero idempotents, whereas the full-GL law has mean one and permits zero. The Wei–Zou classification counts isomorphism classes, not this labeled idempotent distribution. Searches of algebraic records, paper titles and relevant semilinear aliases found no statement that implies the full theorem. Historical priority of an equivalent triangular fixed-space recurrence remains a risk. Van Peski (2024) studies the complete finite-dimensional rank distribution of random strictly triangular matrices; binary-field rank recurrence is not asserted original. The distinctive claim is its nonlinear evolution-algebra interpretation and field-size invariance over all binary extension fields. Full text of this plausible source remained inaccessible, so historical priority is qualified.

value.rationale: Random structure matrices and idempotent statistics are highlighted as important open directions by the 2026 evolution-algebra survey. The natural graph-ordered triangular support class has a radically different idempotent statistic from the unrestricted GL ensemble: always at least one nonzero idempotent, exact distribution independent of all binary extension-field sizes, mean increasing linearly in n and variance binomial(n,2). The exact law predicts every finite-dimensional atom and exposes a trace-Frobenius mechanism not apparent from the survey’s full-GL mean-one argument. This is a motivated structural probability classification for a natural infinite algebra family, not a choice of isolated numerical parameters.
